newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turk Cypriot leader says will meet Clerides.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cypriot leader says will meet Clerides.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash said he would meet Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides in Nicosia next week for talks on the future of the divided island.
Denktash told the Turkish Cypriot BRT television channel on Tuesday night that he would hold talks with old rival Clerides in the residence of U.N. representative Gustave Feissel.
"We will meet in Feissel's house on Monday," he said. "Meetings and contacts between the two leaders are necessary for the peace and harmony of the two communities."

Denktash, who heads a breakaway state recognised only by Turkey, said he would discuss humanitarian issues with Clerides, the leader of a Greek Cypriot administration regarded abroad as the Mediterranean island's only government.

The pair met in New York state earlier this month under the auspices of the United Nations for the first time in three years in an attempt to revive stalled negotiations on Cypriot reunification as a bi-zonal, bi-communal federation.
The Turkish Cypriot north at the weekend celebrated 23 years since mainland Turkish forces invaded Cyprus, dividing the island in two.
Turkey took over the northern third of Cyprus on July 20, 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup backed by the military then ruling Greece.
Turkish Deputy Prime Minister Bulent Ecevit, who ordered the military operation in 1974, on Sunday called for partial integration of north Cyprus with Turkey.
Ecevit said integration of the self-declared Turkish Cypriot state was inevitable after the European Union gave a green light last week to Cyprus for membership and excluded Turkey.

Denktash said he hoped next week's talks with Clerides would help create a better atmosphere ahead of further direct talks with the Greek Cypriot leader planned for Switzerland in mid-August, BRT TV said.
"If the EU suspends or postpones its decision, we can come together and talk," the station quoted him as saying.
